User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want support assignments available only in the coordinator dashboard.
Acceptance Criteria: Support-required events on the event list page do not show dashboard-only assignment controls or trigger the support-staff lookup.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the required event remains visible. Error case: none applies because no support lookup is requested. Boundary case: a support-required event outside the dashboard still has no assignment control.
Pre-Conditions: Coordinator event list receives a support-required event with dashboard=false.
Test Steps: Arrange the event response; act by rendering the event list page; assert the event and absence of assignment controls and staff lookups.
Test Data: Event 11; dashboard=false; technical support required.
Expected Results: The event is visible, assignment controls are absent, and the staff endpoint is not called.
Test Details: Test: Coordinator view 1 AC1 - keeps support assignment controls off the event list page. Happy event visibility and dashboard-only boundary are asserted; error handling is not applicable because no staff request occurs. The absence of the control and endpoint call fails if assignment UI leaks onto the standard list.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to assign available Technical Support Staff to events that require on-site support.
Acceptance Criteria: The dashboard loads assigned events and support staff, then persists the selected complete team for a required event.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a coordinator adds a staff member and the complete selected IDs are persisted. Error case: API failures are covered in the focused assignment component tests. Boundary case: existing assignments remain selected while newly selected staff are added.
Pre-Conditions: Coordinator dashboard receives one assigned event, one unrelated event, and two available technicians.
Test Steps: Arrange the dashboard API responses; act by selecting an additional technician and saving; assert the request, saved feedback, and selected team.
Test Data: Event 7; unrelated event 8; staff IDs 41 and 42.
Expected Results: The assignment request includes both selected IDs and the saved state displays the updated complete team without removing the unrelated event.
Test Details: Test: Coordinator view 1 / Technical Support AC2 - loads events and saves a dashboard assignment. Happy assignment persistence and existing-selection boundary are asserted; save-error behavior is covered by the assignment AC4 test. The payload and checked-state assertions fail if the dashboard hides assignment controls or drops an assigned member; the unrelated-card assertion fails if updating one assignment removes other events.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want event-list loading, empty, and failure states to be distinguishable.
Acceptance Criteria: The event list announces loading, shows the empty state only after an empty response, and does not request staff outside the coordinator dashboard.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a completed empty response shows the empty state. Error case: a distinct event API failure is tested separately. Boundary case: a response without an events array is treated as an empty list only after loading finishes.
Pre-Conditions: Coordinator event request remains pending before resolving to a response without events.
Test Steps: Arrange a held event request; act by rendering and resolving the request; assert loading, empty feedback, count, and no unrelated staff request.
Test Data: Empty response object; coordinator token.
Expected Results: Loading is visible before resolution; afterward the empty state and zero count appear without a support-staff request.
Test Details: Test: Coordinator view 1 AC1 - shows loading and the empty state when no events are returned. Happy empty-state transition, error distinction through its paired case, and missing-array response boundary are asserted. The status, empty-state, and API-call assertions fail if loading is skipped or an empty response triggers an unrelated staff request.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want retrieval failures to be explained rather than mistaken for an empty assignment list.
Acceptance Criteria: A rejected event request displays its error and does not display the no-events message.
Test Scenario: Happy case: valid event rendering is covered by the dashboard assignment case. Error case: a rejected event request exposes its message. Boundary case: the empty state must remain absent after rejection.
Pre-Conditions: The coordinator event endpoint rejects with a readable message.
Test Steps: Arrange a rejected event request; act by rendering the coordinator list; assert the alert and absence of the empty state.
Test Data: Error message Events are unavailable.
Expected Results: The error alert is visible and no empty-list heading is rendered.
Test Details: Test: Coordinator view 1 AC1 - reports event retrieval failures without showing the empty state. Happy rendering is paired with the success case; error and empty-versus-error boundary are asserted. The alert and absent empty-state assertions fail if the catch is removed or failure is rendered as success.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want a support-staff lookup failure isolated to the event that needs support.
Acceptance Criteria: Required events show the staff lookup error while the event remains visible and optional fields use explicit fallbacks.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a required event remains available for review. Error case: a failed staff lookup is shown on that event. Boundary case: a non-required event has no assignment controls and blank title, purpose, or status values use visible fallbacks.
Pre-Conditions: Coordinator dashboard receives one required event and one event without a support requirement; staff lookup rejects.
Test Steps: Arrange event and rejected staff responses; act by rendering the dashboard; assert the event, fallbacks, scoped error, and absent assignment controls for the other event.
Test Data: Events 8 and 9; blank name and purpose; missing status.
Expected Results: The event cards remain visible; missing values display Untitled Event, No purpose provided, and Draft; staff failure is visible only where relevant.
Test Details: Test: Coordinator view 1 AC1 - reports staff lookup failure and renders optional event fallbacks. Happy event display, staff API error, and non-required-event boundary are asserted. The fallback and visibility assertions fail if an error hides valid events or the support requirement is ignored.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want an incomplete support-staff response handled as no available staff.
Acceptance Criteria: A missing staff array does not crash the dashboard or fabricate available technicians.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the event card remains rendered. Error case: no false alert appears for a successful but incomplete response. Boundary case: a response object without staff uses the empty-team message.
Pre-Conditions: Coordinator dashboard receives a required event; staff endpoint resolves without a staff property.
Test Steps: Arrange a response containing no staff array; act by rendering the dashboard; assert the empty-team message and absence of an alert.
Test Data: Event 10; response object without staff.
Expected Results: No Technical Support Staff are available is shown without an error or assignment button.
Test Details: Test: Technical Support AC2 - handles a staff response without a staff list. Happy card rendering, non-error response, and missing-array boundary are asserted. The assertion fails if absent data is treated as an error or the child receives invalid staff data.

User Story: As an Event Organiser, I want my personal event list and dashboard without coordinator-only controls.
Acceptance Criteria: The personal request list and dashboard action remain visible, and coordinator support staff are not requested.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the organiser workspace and dashboard render. Error case: none applies to this role-isolation check. Boundary case: an empty personal list remains valid in both route modes and never triggers coordinator-only data loading.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated user has the event_organiser role and the event response is empty.
Test Steps: Arrange an organiser identity and empty response; act by rendering My Events and rerendering the dashboard; assert both headings and absence of support-staff API calls.
Test Data: Organiser token; empty event list; dashboard false then true.
Expected Results: My Events and Event Organiser Dashboard appear with the request link; no support-staff request is made.
Test Details: Test: Organiser view 1 AC1 - renders the personal list and dashboard without requesting support staff. Happy role-specific workspace, dashboard heading, empty-list boundary, and coordinator-only request isolation are asserted. The headings, link, and call assertions fail if organizer title selection or role isolation changes.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to prevent saving an empty support team.
Acceptance Criteria: The assignment submit control is disabled when no technicians are selected.
Test Scenario: Happy case: an existing selected-team assignment is covered by AC2 success tests. Error case: none applies because the request is blocked before submission. Boundary case: exactly zero selected staff cannot reach the API.
Pre-Conditions: At least one staff member is available and the event currently has no assigned staff.
Test Steps: Arrange an empty selection; act by attempting to submit; assert the disabled control and no API call.
Test Data: Zero selected staff.
Expected Results: The submit control stays disabled and no assignment request is issued.
Test Details: Test: AC2 - prevents saving an assignment when no staff are selected. Happy valid-selection behavior is covered separately; invalid empty selection is the boundary and API-call absence proves the rule. A plausible enabled button or empty payload would fail.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want the current event assignment to replace stale checkbox selections after refreshed data arrives.
Acceptance Criteria: The selected technicians synchronize to the event's latest assignment.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a refreshed assignment is reflected in the controls. Error case: none applies to this prop synchronization check. Boundary case: changing the assigned team removes a previously selected but now unassigned technician.
Pre-Conditions: The component is first rendered with Taylor selected and then receives Morgan as the latest assignment.
Test Steps: Arrange the first assignment; act by toggling a choice and rerendering with refreshed event data; assert the final checkbox states.
Test Data: Taylor ID 41; Morgan ID 42.
Expected Results: Taylor is unchecked and Morgan is checked after the new event assignment is received.
Test Details: Test: AC2 - synchronizes selected staff when the event assignment changes. Happy refreshed state and stale-selection boundary are asserted; error handling is covered by AC4. The checked-state assertions fail if the event prop effect is removed.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to know when no Technical Support Staff are available.
Acceptance Criteria: The assignment form presents an empty availability message and omits unusable controls.
Test Scenario: Happy case: none applies because there are no staff to assign. Error case: none applies to a successful empty staff list. Boundary case: zero available staff renders no submit action.
Pre-Conditions: The event assignment form receives an empty staff array.
Test Steps: Arrange an empty availability list; act by rendering the form; assert the message and absence of the submit button.
Test Data: Empty staff list.
Expected Results: The empty-team explanation is visible and there is no assignment button.
Test Details: Test: AC2 - explains when no Technical Support Staff are available. Empty availability boundary and visible message are asserted; no error case is applicable. The assertions fail if the form renders unusable actions or hides the empty state.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want duplicate edits prevented while an assignment save is in flight.
Acceptance Criteria: The form disables selection controls and the submit button until the save request settles.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a resolved request displays saved feedback. Error case: rejected saves are covered by AC4. Boundary case: a pending request cannot be edited or submitted again.
Pre-Conditions: The assignment API request is held until the test resolves it.
Test Steps: Arrange a pending save; act by checking the in-flight state and then resolving the request; assert disabled controls and saved feedback.
Test Data: Assigned technician Taylor; delayed API response.
Expected Results: The submit button and fieldset are disabled during the request; after resolution the saved confirmation appears.
Test Details: Test: AC2 - disables assignment controls while saving. Happy completion and pending-save boundary are asserted; rejected-save handling is separately tested. The disabled-state and saved-feedback assertions fail if controls remain mutable during a request or the final state is not restored.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want a loading indicator before on-site assignment retrieval finishes.
Acceptance Criteria: A pending request shows loading, then an empty response shows the empty-assignment message and zero count.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the empty response reaches ready state. Error case: the rejected request is covered separately. Boundary case: a response without an events array becomes an empty list rather than remaining loading.
Pre-Conditions: The on-site support request is held and then resolves without an events property.
Test Steps: Arrange a pending request; act by rendering and resolving with an empty response; assert both states in order.
Test Data: Response object without events; zero events.
Expected Results: Loading is announced before resolution, followed by the no-assigned-events message and zero count.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - shows the loading state before an empty support response. Happy ready-state result and missing-array boundary are asserted; error state is covered separately. The ordered status and empty-state assertions fail if loading is skipped or completion is not handled.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want an explanation when my on-site assignments cannot be retrieved.
Acceptance Criteria: A rejected support request displays an accessible error instead of an empty assignment state.
Test Scenario: Happy case: populated event display is covered by AC1 event tests. Error case: the API error appears in an alert. Boundary case: an unavailable result must not be represented as zero assignments.
Pre-Conditions: The on-site support endpoint rejects with a readable message.
Test Steps: Arrange a rejected request; act by rendering the section; assert the error and absence of the empty state.
Test Data: Error message Support assignments are unavailable.
Expected Results: The alert contains the failure message and no empty-list heading appears.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - reports support assignment retrieval failures. Happy populated display is covered separately; error and unavailable-versus-empty boundary are asserted. The alert and absent empty-state assertions fail if errors are silently converted into empty data.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want clear fallbacks for optional event details and to see any details that are available.
Acceptance Criteria: Missing schedule and equipment fields are labelled, while event status, venue, notes, and support details remain visible.
Test Scenario: Happy case: provided status, venue location, equipment notes, and support notes display. Error case: none applies to a successful response. Boundary case: missing name, purpose, date, times, venue location, equipment notes, and support details use explicit fallbacks.
Pre-Conditions: The response contains one partially specified event and one event with no optional details.
Test Steps: Arrange the two event records; act by rendering the section; assert provided details and every fallback in their own event card.
Test Data: Two events; one with equipment notes and support details; one with null equipment list and no notes.
Expected Results: Provided details remain visible; missing values display expected event, date, time, venue, and equipment fallbacks; event count is plural.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - displays event and equipment fallbacks alongside available support details. Happy optional values, absent-data boundary, and event count are asserted; API error is covered by AC1 error test. Each text assertion fails if a conditional fallback or supplied support detail is dropped.

User Story: As a developer maintaining database upgrades, preserve cancellation and equipment-review migrations when adding equipment repair history.
Acceptance Criteria: The migration runner applies the cancellation migration, then the equipment-review migration, and appends equipment repair history as the final migration.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the migration runner submits the existing cancellation and equipment-review SQL in order. Boundary case: equipment repair history is the final SQL migration. Error case: migration execution failures are not exercised by this ordering test.
Pre-Conditions: Migration SQL files exist; the PostgreSQL connection is replaced with an in-memory call recorder.
Test Steps: Arrange a fake client; act by invoking migrate(); assert cancellation precedes equipment review and repair history is last.
Test Data: 012-event-cancellation-notifications.sql; 013-equipment-review-affected-items.sql; 012-equipment-repair-history.sql.
Expected Results: Both preserved migrations are applied and the repair-history migration is applied last.
Test Details: Test: test('migration runner preserves cancellation and equipment-review migrations before appending repair history'). Happy path and append-order boundary are covered; migration-error handling is outside this test. A missing call, reversed order, or later migration after repair history makes an assertion fail. The test was inspected and failed before the fix because cancellation was absent.

User Story: As a database maintainer, rerun migration 006 without rejecting existing cancellation or equipment-status notifications.
Acceptance Criteria: Migration 006 notification constraint permits both event_cancelled and equipment_status_changed while retaining all previously accepted types.
Test Scenario: Happy case: both cancellation and equipment-status types are present. Error case: omitted existing types would fail migration when matching rows exist; this test detects omissions from the list. Boundary case: exact accepted type list is asserted.
Pre-Conditions: The SQL migration file is read as text and its notifications_type_check type list is parsed.
Test Steps: Arrange the migration text; act by extracting accepted types; assert the complete expected type sequence including both requested notification types.
Test Data: event_cancelled; equipment_status_changed; all existing change-request, event decision, and safety types.
Expected Results: Migration 006 allows both existing cancellation notifications and equipment-status notifications when rerun.
Test Details: Test: Migration compatibility - preserves event_cancelled and equipment_status_changed notifications. Happy compatibility case and exact-list boundary are asserted; actual database rejection behavior is not exercised here. The test was inspected and failed before the SQL change because event_cancelled was missing; omission of either notification type causes the equality assertion to fail. Exact updated SQL constraint clause: ALTER TABLE notifications ADD CONSTRAINT notifications_type_check CHECK (type IN ('change_request_submitted', 'change_request_approved', 'change_request_rejected', 'event_details_changed', 'event_approved', 'event_rejected', 'safety_check_recorded', 'event_cancelled', 'equipment_status_changed'));

User Story: As a maintainer, protect repair-history records so they are accessed only through the authorised API.
Acceptance Criteria: Enable row-level security on equipment_status_history and revoke direct privileges from anon and authenticated roles.
Test Scenario: Happy case: migration enables RLS and revokes both browser roles. Error case: omission of any access-control statement leaves a direct access path and fails the assertion. Boundary case: role existence is guarded so migration can run where either role is absent.
Pre-Conditions: The migration SQL is read from disk; PostgreSQL is not needed for this static regression check.
Test Steps: Arrange by loading the SQL; act by checking the migration text; assert RLS and each guarded revoke are present.
Test Data: equipment_status_history; anon; authenticated.
Expected Results: RLS is enabled and direct privileges are revoked from anon and authenticated, leaving API-mediated access.
Test Details: Test: AC4 - enables RLS and revokes anon and authenticated access to repair history. The test was inspected and failed before the SQL change because RLS was absent. Missing RLS or either revoke makes an assertion fail. No SQL behavior is uncovered by this static check, though a live database permission test is not included.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, repair unavailable equipment so it can be reserved for a new reviewed event and retain the resolution note in its history.
Acceptance Criteria: After repair, the asset is eligible for a new reservation and the exact repair resolution note is persisted in equipment_status_history.
Test Scenario: Happy case: repair the unavailable fixture asset through the authenticated API, then reserve it through the real API and verify durable audit and reservation rows. Error cases and boundary cases are outside this one happy-path regression.
Pre-Conditions: RUN_DB_TESTS=1 and a PostgreSQL connection are required; the test creates a random disposable schema, applies real migrations, and removes the schema afterward.
Test Steps: Arrange users, an unavailable asset, a future availability slot, and a fully reviewed event; act by repairing and creating the reservation; assert the reservation and exact repair history record in PostgreSQL.
Test Data: Unavailable one-unit projector; future date at CURRENT_DATE + 30; resolution note 'Replaced the damaged lamp and passed the projection test.'
Expected Results: Repair returns Available; reservation API returns 201 for the exact asset; PostgreSQL contains the available-status history row with the resolution note and staff identity.
Test Details: Test: AC1-AC2 - repaired equipment can be reserved and its resolution note persists in PostgreSQL history. Inspected; the successful API reservation fails if repaired inventory remains ineligible, and the database equality assertions fail if the note, status, or staff identity is not persisted. Happy path only; no error or boundary scenario is included. The test is opt-in and was not run against the configured non-local database.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC1
User Story: As a Technical Support Staff, I want to be alerted when previously reserved equipment becomes unavailable so that I can source a replacement or notify the Event Coordinator in time.
Acceptance Criteria: Marking an asset unavailable records its reason, flags every upcoming confirmed reservation containing it, and alerts the event's assigned support staff and Coordinator.
Test Scenario: Happy case: more than one future reserved allocation is affected and each event's assigned team and Coordinator are notified. Error case: a previously changed asset cannot be marked unavailable twice. Boundary case: completed or past reservations are excluded.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated Technical Support session; database pool replaced by a transaction recorder returning impacted future reserved allocations.
Test Steps: Arrange an available inventory asset and several future reservation rows; act by marking it unavailable; assert issue rows, history, recipient IDs, and transaction commit.
Test Data: Asset PROJ-001; damaged reason; two active reservations across distinct events.
Expected Results: Each affected future reservation receives an open issue and both assigned recipient audiences receive notifications in the same committed transaction; unrelated and past allocations are not flagged.
Test Details: Test: 'AC1 AC3 AC4 - flags each affected confirmed reservation and notifies assigned support and Coordinator'. Happy multiple-recipient behavior and invalid-reason boundaries are covered; live PostgreSQL behavior is not exercised. The assertions fail if the affected query omits active allocations, notifications omit either recipient class, or the audit/issue transaction does not commit.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC1
User Story: As a Technical Support Staff, I want to record why equipment is unavailable so that the impact can be understood and audited.
Acceptance Criteria: Unavailability reports require a non-empty reason of at most 500 characters and a valid inventory identifier.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a valid reason is accepted. Error cases: blank, whitespace-only, and overlong reasons are rejected before transaction access. Boundary case: the 500-character maximum is enforced.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated Technical Support API route; a mocked pool connect detects accidental transaction starts.
Test Steps: Arrange invalid reason values; act by PUT to the asset unavailable endpoint; assert HTTP 400 and zero transaction opens.
Test Data: Blank; whitespace; 501-character reason; positive inventory ID.
Expected Results: Invalid reports produce a client error and cannot alter inventory or audit history.
Test Details: Test: 'AC1 - rejects blank or overlong unavailability reasons before writing'. Error and length boundary cases are explicit. The connect-call assertion fails if invalid input reaches persistence; the valid 500-character maximum is accepted by controller validation but not separately exercised.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC2
User Story: As assigned Technical Support Staff, I want to view every reservation affected by unavailable equipment so that I can coordinate a replacement.
Acceptance Criteria: The support issue list is restricted to open issues on events assigned to the authenticated staff member.
Test Scenario: Happy case: assigned staff receive the issue list. Error/security case: an unassigned staff member has no matching assignment rows. Boundary case: resolved issues and non-reserved allocations are excluded.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated Technical Support identity and an intercepted read query.
Test Steps: Arrange a Technical Support identity; act by requesting the affected reservation queue; assert the staff ID is a bound assignment filter and only returned rows are exposed.
Test Data: Staff ID 41 and issue ID 601.
Expected Results: Only events joined to the signed-in staff assignment are listed; other event issues cannot be disclosed.
Test Details: Test: 'AC2 - lists affected reservations only through the signed-in member event assignment'. Security and status filters are checked in the query; a missing staff predicate or wrong bound ID fails. A live authorization database policy is not needed because API roles and record scoping are tested at the route/model boundary.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC3
User Story: As assigned Technical Support Staff, I want to propose a replacement selection so the Coordinator can decide whether to update the reservation.
Acceptance Criteria: A proposal must be for an available same-type asset with enough stock for the complete reservation slot and notifies the assigned Coordinator; the original reservation remains unchanged pending a decision.
Test Scenario: Happy case: valid replacement proposal persists with the affected quantity and Coordinator notification. Error cases: wrong equipment type, unavailable/insufficient stock, and duplicate pending proposal are refused. Boundary case: the entire event interval and full affected quantity are checked.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated staff assigned to the event; transaction client returns issue, alternative stock, and slot availability.
Test Steps: Arrange an open issue and candidate replacement; act by POSTing the candidate; assert proposal row, quantity, Coordinator notification, and no original reservation item deletion.
Test Data: Issue 601; one Projector; alternative asset 92 available for the event slot.
Expected Results: A pending proposal is stored and notified, but equipment lines remain unchanged until Coordinator acceptance.
Test Details: Test: 'AC3 AC4 - stores the replacement proposal and notifies the assigned Coordinator'; 'AC3 - refuses a proposal for a different equipment type without storing it'; 'AC3 - refuses a proposal for an unavailable or insufficient asset without storing it'. Happy, error, and quantity/slot boundary paths are represented; live concurrent PostgreSQL contention is not exercised. A wrong type, insufficient stock, missing notice, or premature reservation swap fails these assertions.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC3
User Story: As assigned Technical Support Staff, I want proposals reviewed by the event's assigned Coordinator so the correct event owner controls reservation changes.
Acceptance Criteria: Only the assigned Event Coordinator can read or decide a proposal for the event.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the assigned Coordinator can retrieve the issue and decide it. Error/security case: a different Coordinator receives not found and causes no writes. Boundary case: an invalid proposal identifier is rejected before lookup.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated Coordinator session; database query returns no matching coordinator-scoped proposal.
Test Steps: Arrange a Coordinator not assigned to the proposal event; act by submitting an accept decision; assert 404 and no reservation or notification write.
Test Data: Coordinator ID 30; proposal ID 701; event coordinator ID differs.
Expected Results: The proposal remains unchanged and no private event details or write effects are returned.
Test Details: Test: 'AC3 - hides a proposal from a Coordinator who is not assigned to its event'. The no-row query result and absent update assertion fail if event scoping is removed or a foreign coordinator can decide.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC3-AC4
User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to accept a proposed alternative and update the reservation so the event remains equipped.
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance atomically replaces the affected reserved item, resolves the issue, records the decision, and notifies assigned support.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a still-available alternative is accepted and reservation lines are replaced. Error case: a proposal whose stock became unavailable is refused with no partial write. Boundary case: merging with an already-selected same-type asset preserves aggregate quantity.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated assigned Coordinator and transaction client for reservation, stock, proposal, and issue records.
Test Steps: Arrange a pending proposal and available replacement; act by accepting; assert delete/upsert, resolved issue, accepted proposal, notification, and commit as one transaction.
Test Data: Reservation 901; old inventory 91; replacement 92; quantity 1.
Expected Results: Reservation now references the alternative, the issue is resolved, and assigned support receives the decision.
Test Details: Test: 'AC3 AC4 - Coordinator accepted decision updates the reservation'. The test inspects writes and commit; it fails if the unavailable item remains, the issue is not resolved, or support is not notified. The merged-existing-line and live stock-race branches are protected in SQL but not exercised by this mocked transaction test.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC3-AC4
User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to reject a proposed alternative when it is unsuitable so Technical Support can suggest another.
Acceptance Criteria: Rejection records the decision, keeps the unavailability issue open, and notifies assigned support so another proposal can be made.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the pending proposal is rejected and support is notified. Error case: an already-decided proposal cannot be decided again. Boundary case: rejecting does not remove or substitute the originally reserved line.
Pre-Conditions: Authenticated assigned Coordinator; mock transaction contains a pending proposal.
Test Steps: Arrange an open issue and pending alternative; act by rejecting; assert decision update and notification without reservation-item or issue-resolution writes.
Test Data: Proposal 701; decision 'rejected'.
Expected Results: The original reservation remains flagged/open and support can submit another proposal.
Test Details: Test: 'AC3 AC4 - Coordinator rejected decision keeps the issue open'. The explicit absence of reservation and issue-resolved writes fails if rejection accidentally updates or closes the reservation.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC1-AC4
User Story: As a maintainer, I want reservation incident/proposal records and notification types installed safely so the workflow persists across deployments.
Acceptance Criteria: The final migration creates secured incident/proposal tables, permits the new notification types, and runs after prior migrations.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the migration runner applies every migration in the required sequence. Error/security case: direct browser-role table access is revoked. Boundary case: notification constraints retain previously accepted types while adding the workflow types.
Pre-Conditions: Read migration SQL and invoke migration runner against a transaction-call recorder; no live database is used.
Test Steps: Arrange migration files and recorder; act by running migrate(); assert the new migration is final and SQL contains RLS, revokes, and notification types.
Test Data: Migration 014; incident/proposal tables; three new notification types.
Expected Results: Migration ordering and access-control declarations are checked and all old notification types remain accepted.
Test Details: Tests: 'AC3 AC4 migration - secures workflow records and permits its notification types'; 'migration runner preserves previous migrations before appending reservation unavailability'; 'Migration compatibility - preserves event_cancelled and equipment_status_changed notifications'. Happy migration order and error/security/compatibility cases are covered; live PostgreSQL migration execution is not run against the configured shared database. Missing RLS/revokes/types or incorrect order fails an assertion.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC1
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want to record an equipment unavailability reason in the inventory workspace so that affected reservations are detected.
Acceptance Criteria: A non-empty reason is required before inventory is marked unavailable.
Test Scenario: Happy case: a trimmed valid reason is submitted. Error case: an empty reason leaves the API untouched. Boundary case: whitespace-only input is not accepted.
Pre-Conditions: Render the inventory UI with one available asset and a callback spy.
Test Steps: Arrange available item; act by opening the form, submitting blank, then entering a padded reason; assert validation and the trimmed callback value.
Test Data: Asset PROJ-001; reason 'Damaged during setup'.
Expected Results: No write occurs for blank input; valid reason is passed to the mark-unavailable action.
Test Details: Test: 'AC1 - requires a reason and submits the equipment unavailability report'. Happy, error, and blank boundary are distinct. The callback assertion fails if the action bypasses validation or persists untrimmed text.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC2-AC3
User Story: As assigned Technical Support Staff, I want to inspect affected reservations and submit an alternative for Coordinator review.
Acceptance Criteria: The support workspace displays unavailable reservation details and offers only returned available alternatives.
Test Scenario: Happy case: event, old asset, reason, slot, and candidate appear; support submits one replacement. Error case: API failure remains visible. Boundary case: no available alternatives prevents submission.
Pre-Conditions: Render affected reservations with a candidate and mocked authenticated API client.
Test Steps: Arrange an affected issue; act by submitting a candidate, submitting with no selection, and rendering no candidates; assert endpoint and user-facing outcomes.
Test Data: Issue 601; replacement ID 92; empty alternative list.
Expected Results: The selected alternative is sent and the workspace refreshes; missing selection is rejected locally; no candidates disable submission.
Test Details: Tests: 'AC2 AC3 - shows the affected reservation and submits its alternative proposal'; 'AC3 - displays a replacement proposal failure'; 'AC3 - requires a replacement selection before sending a proposal'; 'AC3 - blocks a proposal without an available alternative'. Happy, error, and boundary cases are distinct; the exact payload, visible failure, and disabled/validation behavior fail if the wrong asset is sent or invalid submissions reach the API.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC4
User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to accept the proposed alternative from the event page so the reservation can be updated.
Acceptance Criteria: The Coordinator can accept a pending proposal and sees the refreshed resolved issue list.
Test Scenario: Happy case: accepting sends the decision and removes the resolved issue after reload. Error case: decision failures remain visible. Boundary case: only pending proposals offer action controls.
Pre-Conditions: Render the assigned event issue section with pending, empty-proposal, and malformed API responses.
Test Steps: Arrange pending proposals; act by accepting, returning malformed issue data, and rejecting decisions; assert request, refresh, and visible error/no-proposal states.
Test Data: Event 501; proposal 701.
Expected Results: The API receives accepted and the event detail refreshes; malformed and failed responses remain visibly errored; empty proposal state is explained.
Test Details: Tests: 'AC4 - accepts the proposal from the event page and reloads the issue list'; 'AC4 - reports malformed affected-reservation data from the event API'; 'AC4 - explains when Technical Support has not proposed an alternative'; 'AC4 - keeps a proposal available and reports failed Coordinator decisions'. Happy, error, and empty boundary cases are distinct; assertions fail if the event page hides malformed data, silently succeeds, or omits refreshed state.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC4
User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to reject a proposed alternative and leave the issue visible for Technical Support to retry.
Acceptance Criteria: Rejecting sends the decision and keeps the unresolved issue visible.
Test Scenario: Happy case: reject sends the correct decision and refreshed issue shows rejected status. Error case: API errors are surfaced. Boundary case: an issue without a pending proposal has no decision controls.
Pre-Conditions: Render an issue with a pending proposal and return the rejected proposal on refresh; also simulate a failed decision.
Test Steps: Arrange pending proposal; act by selecting Reject alternative and by causing decision failures; assert decision payload, retained issue, and error.
Test Data: Event 501; proposal 701.
Expected Results: The issue remains visible and the selected proposal displays rejected; failed decisions leave the pending proposal available.
Test Details: Tests: 'AC4 - rejects the proposal without hiding the affected reservation'; 'AC4 - keeps a proposal available and reports failed Coordinator decisions'. Happy, error, and pending-state boundary cases are distinct; the exact rejected state and retained controls fail if rejection hides the incident or failures are presented as success.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC1
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want a failed unavailability update explained so I can correct the reason and retry.
Acceptance Criteria: A failed inventory update displays an error and editing the reason clears the stale error.
Test Scenario: Happy case: correction clears the prior error. Error case: a rejected update with no message uses the visible fallback. Boundary case: the failed update must not appear successful.
Pre-Conditions: Render an available asset with a rejecting unavailability callback.
Test Steps: Arrange available inventory; act by submitting a reason that fails, then edit the reason; assert fallback and error clearance.
Test Data: Asset PROJ-001; reason 'Damaged during setup'.
Expected Results: The user sees the fallback error, no success state, and an updated reason clears the stale error.
Test Details: Test: 'AC1 - displays an unavailability failure and clears it when the reason changes'. Happy recovery, error, and rejected-save boundary are distinct; missing catch/error-reset behavior fails the accessible alert assertions.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC3
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want pending proposals protected from duplicate submissions and a clear response to invalid or failed proposals.
Acceptance Criteria: Pending proposal status is read-only; empty selection is rejected and an API failure is visible.
Test Scenario: Happy case: pending state prevents duplicate proposals. Error case: proposal API failure is visible. Boundary case: empty selection does not reach the API.
Pre-Conditions: Render affected issue cards with pending, no-choice, and available-alternative configurations.
Test Steps: Arrange each proposal state; act by submitting an empty choice or failed request; assert displayed state and endpoint behavior.
Test Data: Issue 601; proposal 701; replacement ID 92.
Expected Results: Pending proposals expose no send control; empty selection is rejected locally; failed sends show an error.
Test Details: Tests: 'AC3 - keeps a pending replacement proposal read-only for Technical Support'; 'AC3 - requires a replacement selection before sending a proposal'; 'AC3 - displays a replacement proposal failure'. Happy, error, and boundary cases are distinct; assertions fail if a duplicate proposal is enabled, empty selection reaches the API, or failure is hidden.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC1-AC3
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want unavailability and replacement actions to refresh the dashboard and surface their outcomes.
Acceptance Criteria: After equipment is marked unavailable, inventory and issue data refresh; after a proposal is sent, the dashboard confirms the Coordinator handoff.
Test Scenario: Happy case: inventory status and affected reservations refresh. Error case: component-level failures remain visible. Boundary case: the flagged issue count is reflected in feedback.
Pre-Conditions: Render the authenticated dashboard with mocked API data and trigger each workflow action.
Test Steps: Arrange dashboard API responses; act by marking an item unavailable and sending a replacement; assert API request, refreshed status, and user-facing confirmation.
Test Data: Support token; PROJ-001; one affected issue; issue 601; replacement 92.
Expected Results: Inventory reflects Unavailable, issue data refreshes, and both actions show specific success feedback.
Test Details: Tests: 'AC1-AC3 - marks equipment unavailable and reports how many reservations were flagged'; 'AC3 - refreshes affected reservations after a replacement proposal is sent'. Happy dashboard flows are distinct by action; the request, resulting inventory, flagged count, and toast assertions fail if the dashboard callback is disconnected or stale state is shown.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC3
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want to revise a replacement after the Coordinator rejects it.
Acceptance Criteria: A rejected proposal is visible and the assigned Support member may submit another available alternative.
Test Scenario: Happy case: support sees rejected proposal and sends a new candidate. Error case: proposal endpoint failures remain visible. Boundary case: a pending proposal, unlike a rejected one, is read-only.
Pre-Conditions: Render one affected reservation with a rejected proposal and one available alternative.
Test Steps: Arrange rejected proposal; act by choosing the alternative and resubmitting; assert the replacement request and successful callback path.
Test Data: Issue 601; rejected proposal PROJ-002; replacement ID 92.
Expected Results: The rejected proposal remains visible and the updated candidate can be submitted for review.
Test Details: Test: 'AC3 - shows a rejected proposal and allows Technical Support to retry'. Happy retry and pending-state boundary are distinct; the exact payload assertion fails if retries are blocked or target the wrong item.

Story/AC: Handle Equipment Unavailability After Reservation / AC4
User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want an explanation when affected reservation details cannot be loaded.
Acceptance Criteria: The event issue panel displays a fallback when the service returns an unstructured load failure.
Test Scenario: Happy case: valid issue data renders in adjacent AC4 tests. Error case: an unstructured transport rejection produces an accessible fallback. Boundary case: the error has no message.
Pre-Conditions: Render the event issue panel with the issue endpoint rejecting an empty object.
Test Steps: Arrange an unstructured API failure; act by rendering the event panel; assert the accessible fallback message.
Test Data: Event 501; rejected value without message.
Expected Results: The Coordinator sees 'Unable to load affected reservations.' instead of an empty or success-shaped panel.
Test Details: Test: 'AC4 - reports a fallback when affected reservations cannot be loaded'. Error and missing-message boundary are distinct; the alert assertion fails if the failure is silently swallowed or produces a blank message.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want to change equipment availability through a compact dropdown without losing the audit safeguards.
Acceptance Criteria: The dropdown reflects the current Available/Unavailable state; an unsubmitted transition can be cancelled by returning to the current value; reasons remain required for completed transitions.
Test Scenario: Happy case: current status and the two valid options are displayed. Error case: empty reasons do not persist a change. Boundary case: selecting the current state cancels without an API call.
Pre-Conditions: Render one available asset with the status-change handler.
Test Steps: Arrange the inventory row; act by selecting Unavailable then restoring Available before entering a reason; assert current value, options, removed form, and no callback.
Test Data: Asset PROJ-001; statuses Available and Unavailable.
Expected Results: The select shows the actual status, offers only the supported choices, and cancelling returns to the original state without persisting.
Test Details: Tests: 'UI AC1 - shows the current status and cancels a pending change when reset'; 'AC1 - requires a reason and submits the equipment unavailability report'; 'AC1 - maps legacy maintenance status to Unavailable'. Happy, error, and boundary cases are distinct. Assertions fail if the dropdown options/current value are wrong, cancellation triggers a write, or legacy unavailable equipment appears available.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want to review prior availability changes so I can understand why an asset was withdrawn or restored.
Acceptance Criteria: Each recorded transition, its audit note, and its date remain visible in a clearly separated history entry.
Test Scenario: Happy case: previous unavailability reason and repair resolution and both dates remain visible after repair. Error and boundary cases are not applicable to this display-only audit assertion.
Pre-Conditions: Render an unavailable asset with an existing status-history entry; return the repaired asset with the appended resolution entry.
Test Steps: Arrange existing damage history; act by completing the repair; assert both old and new history entries, reasons, dates, and staff attribution are readable separately.
Test Data: Unavailable changed on 10 Oct 2026; Available changed on 17 Oct 2026; staff Taylor Support.
Expected Results: Each history entry is a separate compact card with a status badge and abbreviated date in its header, reason on its own line, and staff attribution as secondary metadata.
Test Details: Test: 'AC4 - shows the updated status and resolution note in equipment history'. Happy audit entries include old/new reasons, dates, actor, and distinct unavailable/available badge classes; error and boundary cases are not applicable to this read-only display assertion. Assertions fail if entries are omitted, merged, dates hidden, or either status gets the wrong badge treatment.

User Story: As a maintainer, I want the Technical Support assignment migration to be safely repeatable in an isolated schema so deployments preserve assignment notifications and restrict browser-role access.
Acceptance Criteria: Rerunning the migration in the active schema preserves assignment notification records, and browser roles cannot read the assignment table.
Test Scenario: Happy case: an assignment notification survives a repeated migration. Error/security case: browser roles are denied assignment-table access. Boundary case: the active disposable schema lacks is_read even when public.notifications has that column, and rerunning the migration still succeeds.
Pre-Conditions: PostgreSQL is available; the test creates a disposable schema with users, events, and notifications tables, then runs the real migration.
Test Steps: Arrange an isolated non-public schema; act by applying the migration, inserting an assignment notification, and applying the migration again; assert the notification remains and available browser roles cannot select assignments.
Test Data: Disposable schema notifications table without is_read; notification type technical_support_assigned; browser roles anon and authenticated when present.
Expected Results: The migration changes only the notifications table in the active schema, reruns successfully, preserves the notification, and denies browser-role reads of event assignments.
Test Details: Test: 'AC3 migration - assignment notifications survive migration reruns and browser roles cannot read assignments'. Happy persistence, error/security access denial, and schema-boundary idempotence are all asserted. The original failure was caused by a public-schema lookup incorrectly changing a different schema's notifications table; the test would fail if the migration again selected public.notifications metadata.
